correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the lift to the finite permutation skew product of arXiv:2609.01140v1. A lifted word is determined by a base word and an initial fiber state. Linear recurrence controls return-word lengths uniformly; inducing on the corresponding cylinder gives a minimal finite permutation extension of a derived shift; the finite-derived-system/fiber argument used in arXiv:2602.13652v1 gives a cylinder-independent bound in return-word time. Multiplication by the base return-length bound yields a global linear recurrence constant. Periodic and higher-block cases are explicitly accounted for.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies linear recurrence, rather than substitutional origin, as the substantive recurrence hypothesis preserved by minimal permutative lifts. It supplies a reusable permanence result for a natural finite-extension construction, immediately preserves unique ergodicity, and broadens a recent primitive-substitution statement without introducing an arbitrary parameter slice or routine numerical refinement.
